g.text: Every rule is a hidden ρ
ρ = how much the two systems’ scores move together, question by question.
Pick a rule and you have picked a ρ — whether you meant to or not.
Every question that is hard for one system is
hard for the other. The shared difficulty cancels
— this is the best pairing can ever do.
This is what the actual rule assumes.
One system’s easy questions are the other’s
hard ones. The worst case — and exactly rule 3.
σΔ can only land in this band — and each rule sits at one point in it
min(σA, σB) if EITHER mean escapes
In practice ρ > 0 — the same hard questions hurt both systems — so the truth sits left of ρ = 0. Pairing the answers measures it instead of assuming it.
Rules 1 & 2 treat σΔ as max(σA, σB) · Rule 3 treats it as σA + σB · The actual rule treats it as √(σA² + σB²)
Three rules, one formula, three different assumptions about ρ.
